Axiom: Complexity — branching, indirection, state held in memory, number of concepts a reader must hold at once — is a budget spent against the problem's ACTUAL shape, not the imagined future one. Judge whether the complexity the diff adds is proportional to what today's requirement needs; generality/config/abstraction built for a need that is not yet real is over-spend, flagged regardless of how clean the code looks in isolation. This is a language-independent practice no linter measures — it is read from the diff against the stated problem, not from style rules.
